resume: Findings in `unverified` with `refutersDispatched` above `refutersInconclusive` lost a refuter to a crash — a pair whose every vote died was re-dispatched once in-run and died again — and no refuter that ran decided them. Defer them as crashed — reported, not acted on: omp's eval has no cached-replay mechanism, so a fresh review re-dispatches every agent() live rather than only the crashed legs, and the in-run retry was this review's one re-dispatch. Re-run nothing for them.
testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

survived.claim: Since this PR, the sweep throws `unbalanced bracket at offset 0` on valid JS `for ([x]of y)` or `for ({…}of y)` (no space before `of`) in any module where a traced variable makes shape() run. On base the same source returns a result.
survived.evidence: In a PROBE3 test appended to the head file, sweep({"x.mjs": MOD(`let T = 20_000;\nfor ([T]of [[1]]);\nspawnSync("gh", ["x"], { timeout: T });`)}) threw `Error: unbalanced bracket at offset 0 at closing → pieces → walk → shape`. The same source run against the base file (reverse-applied diff, zz-base2.test.mjs) returned `[[null,true,[],0]]`, and so did `for ({ a: T }of …)`. Cause: topLevel() turns nested brackets into spaces, so `/\s(?:of|in)\s/` matches one character early and the lhs becomes `[T` with no closing bracket.
survived.suggested_fix: Locate `of`/`in` with a word-boundary match on the unblanked top-level text, for example `/(?<![\w$])(?:of|in)(?![\w$])/` checked against the depth-1 positions. Or slice the lhs at the start of the keyword, not at the whitespace before it.

The spaced control `for ([T] of [[1]])` returned a normal result, so the missing space before `of` is what triggers it. I did not re-run the base-side comparison. survived.claim: Rule 5 misses a destructuring assignment that directly follows `)` or a keyword: `if (c) [T] = [env];`, `else [T] = [env];` and `return [T] = [env];` are accepted with no refusal. shape() treats a `[` after `[\w$)\]]` as an index access.
survived.evidence: PROBE output at head: `if-head then array pattern => [[null,true,[],0]]`, `else then array pattern => [[null,true,[],0]]`, `return array pattern => [[null,true,[],0]]`. The control `[T] = [env]` gives `["T is a destructuring target…"]`, and `void ([T] = [env])` is also refused. `for (const x of [1]) [T] = [env];` is accepted as well (PROBE2 `for-of body array pattern => [[null,true,[],0]]`).
survived.suggested_fix: Before taking `[` as an index, check whether the `)` closes an if/while/for/with head (parenKind), and whether the word before `[` is a keyword (the PREFIXED list: return/else/do/case/…).

survived.claim: The return value of Object.assign() is the target object, but handingAt() returns null for any Object.assign argument. So `const o2 = Object.assign(opts, {}); o2.timeout = env;` and `Object.assign(opts, {}).timeout = env;` lengthen the gh timeout and are accepted.
survived.evidence: PROBE at head: `Object.assign source bound` (WITH_OPTS-style source `const o2 = Object.assign(opts, {});\no2.timeout = ENV_MS;` then spawnSync("gh", ["x"], opts)) => [[null,true,[],0]]. PROBE2 `Object.assign result member write` => [[null,true,[],0]].
survived.suggested_fix: For the first argument, return null only when the Object.assign call is an expression statement. Otherwise, judge the call's own position (bound/returned/passed) the way a bare name is judged.

votes.reason: Claim confirmed. Probe appended to the test file in my own measure-copy, using the test's own sweep() and WITH_OPTS. Both `const o2 = Object.assign(opts, {}); o2.timeout = ENV_MS;` and `Object.assign(opts, {}).timeout = ENV_MS;` gave reaches [[]] with 0 problems, so the gh spawn is accepted. The positive control `opts.timeout = ENV_MS;` gave ["reads process.env.TICKETLESS_TIMEOUT"], so the sweep does detect the env read when the write is direct. Probe run: node --test --test-name-pattern=PROBE tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs → exit 0, tests 1, pass 1. This is a probe, not a red test. unverified.claim: Rule 7 claims writes are looked for in every module that imports the object, but a third module that takes it through a namespace destructure (`const { CFG } = ns; CFG.ms = env;`) or through a plain re-export of an import (`import { CFG } from "./common.mjs"; export { CFG };`, imported elsewhere) can write it unseen.
unverified.evidence: PROBE at head: `namespace destructured` (y.mjs: `import * as ns from "./common.mjs";\nconst { CFG } = ns;\nCFG.ms = ENV;`, x.mjs reads CFG.ms) => [[null,true,[],0]]. PROBE2 `plain re-export of an import` (y.mjs: `import { CFG } from "./common.mjs"; export { CFG };`, z.mjs: `import { CFG } from "./y.mjs"; CFG.ms = ENV;`) => [[null,true,[],0]]. places() only follows imports resolving to the home module, and handingAt() returns null for `export { CFG }` and never looks at bare `ns` occurrences.
unverified.suggested_fix: Treat `ns` as a handed-on name when it appears other than as `ns.X` (destructure, bind, or call argument). In elsewhere(), refuse a module that both imports the name and lists it in `export { … }`, or follow re-exports transitively in places().

unverified.claim: handingAt() returns null for any name whose innermost bracket is a pattern, so a name inside a pattern default expression is missed: `const [a = c ? 1 : opts] = []; a.timeout = env;` binds `a` to opts and is accepted.
unverified.evidence: PROBE at head: `pattern default with ternary hands on` => [[null,true,[],0]].
unverified.suggested_fix: In the pattern-entry branch, require that the occurrence be the entry's target (before any top-level `=` of the entry). Do not exempt names in its default.

unverified.claim: Some writes through another name remain unseen. unverified.evidence: PROBE at head: `method on object writes this => [[null,true,[],0]]`, `namespace handed to function => [[null,true,[],0]]`. The base run of the same probes gave identical output.

unverified.claim: Several uses that the header says are not handed on are refused anyway (fail-closed false positives that could fail the plugin/scripts sweep on future code): an unparenthesised arrow parameter of the object's name, a function-local `const opts` shadowing a module one, and a spread written with a space (`{ ... opts }`).
unverified.evidence: PROBE at head: `[1].map(opts => 1)` => reaches ["…opts is passed to .map(…)…"], while the parenthesised form is in the PR's accepted list. `function f() { const opts = {}; log(opts); }` => ["…passed to log(…)…"]. `log({ ... opts })` => ["…passed to log(…)…"], while `...opts` is skipped by occurrences()' lookbehind.
unverified.suggested_fix: Recognise `name =>` as params, skip occurrences under a nearer `const/let/var` binding of the name (as declRefs scopes do), and allow whitespace after `...` in occurrences().

unverified.claim: No scope creep found: the diff touches only tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs, which is the file the Agent Brief names. Moving splitDefault() to module level is needed so shape()/walk() can use it outside tracer().
The new handed-on regex `/^(?:new\b|Object\s*\.\s*(?:assign|create|fromEntries)\s*\()/` is only partly pinned: removing the `new\b` alternative, or the `create` alternative, leaves every test green.
unverified.evidence: Mutants applied in the copy: `new\b|` removed, and `create|` removed. `node --test tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs` → exit 0, no failing test, both times (baseline: exit 0, tests 25 pass 25). Removing the whole Object.assign/create/fromEntries alternative or the handedOn() call does turn 'the sweep refuses a gh timeout an object it reads is handed on' red. Inconclusive for a kill; no valid red exists for these two mutants.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add refused cases for `new X({...opts})` in a value position and for `Object.create(...)`/`Object.fromEntries(...)` carrying the object, or drop the unneeded alternatives.
